519: /// Keeps track of whether we are currently visiting a class or function definition in a
520: /// [`LogicalLine`]. If we are visiting a class or function, the struct also keeps track
521: /// of the [type parameters] of the class/function.
522: ///
523: /// Call [`LogicalLine::visit_token_kind`] on the [`TokenKind`] of each
524: /// successive [`LogicalLineToken`] to ensure the state remains up to date.
525: ///
526: /// [type parameters]: https://docs.python.org/3/reference/compound_stmts.html#type-params
527: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
528: struct DefinitionState {
529:     in_class: bool,
530:     in_function: bool,
531:     in_type_alias: bool,
532:     type_params: TypeParamsState,
533: }
534: 
535: impl DefinitionState {
536:     fn not_in_definition() -> Self {
537:         Self {
538:             in_class: false,
539:             in_function: false,
540:             in_type_alias: false,
541:             type_params: TypeParamsState::default(),
542:         }
543:     }
544: 
545:     fn from_tokens<'a>(tokens: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a LogicalLineToken>) -> Self {
546:         let mut token_kinds = tokens.into_iter().map(LogicalLineToken::kind);
547:         while let Some(token_kind) = token_kinds.next() {
548:             match token_kind {
549:                 TokenKind::Indent | TokenKind::Dedent => continue,
550:                 TokenKind::Class => {
551:                     return Self {
552:                         in_class: true,
553:                         in_function: false,
554:                         in_type_alias: false,
555:                         type_params: TypeParamsState::default(),
556:                     };
557:                 }
558:                 TokenKind::Def => {
559:                     return Self {
560:                         in_class: false,
561:                         in_function: true,
562:                         in_type_alias: false,
563:                         type_params: TypeParamsState::default(),
564:                     };
565:                 }
566:                 TokenKind::Async if matches!(token_kinds.next(), Some(TokenKind::Def)) => {
567:                     return Self {
568:                         in_class: false,
569:                         in_function: true,
570:                         in_type_alias: false,
571:                         type_params: TypeParamsState::default(),
572:                     };
573:                 }
574:                 TokenKind::Type => {
575:                     return Self {
576:                         in_class: false,
577:                         in_function: false,
578:                         in_type_alias: true,
579:                         type_params: TypeParamsState::default(),
580:                     };
581:                 }
582:                 _ => return Self::not_in_definition(),
583:             }

part.text:
Fixed. The root cause: in `DefinitionState`'s token-walking state machine, a `[` in a type alias like `type MyType = Annotated[...]` was mistaken for the opening of a PEP 695 type-parameter list, so `in_type_params()` stayed true and every `=` in the aliased value (e.g., `pydantic.Field(min_length=4, ...)`) was flagged as E252 — twice per occurrence (once for missing space before, once after).

The fix (crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pycodestyle/rules/logical_lines/mod.rs:241): when an `Equal` token appears while `before_type_params` is still set, treat it as the type-alias assignment `=`, mark the type-parameter list as ended, and never treat subsequent brackets as type params. Valid cases like `type Coro[T: object = Any] = ...` are unaffected because `before_type_params` is already cleared once the real type-param brackets open.

Verified: `cargo test -p ruff_linter --lib` — 2221 passed (including the E252 snapshot test), and the issue's reproducer now reports `All checks passed!`.
